task.description: Validate the fix design at src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md for ISS-0107 / GitHub #366 before BACKEND-DEV implements it. Hard gate: implementation must not start until this returns PASS.
acceptance_criteria: Design addresses the diagnosed root_cause in docs/issues/ISS-0107.json: widen the existing advisory-lock critical section in TestHarness.init() to cover resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims(), not a workaround
All structural changes documented precisely enough for BACKEND-DEV to implement without ambiguity (exact current lock acquire/release points, exact new release point)
No implementation code present (no literal Zig diff)
Lock-key reuse decision (same key vs distinct) is justified
Serialization/performance tradeoff explicitly acknowledged and accepted, not glossed over
Error taxonomy section present (even if none)
Callers/scripts impacted correctly identified as all ~19+ test-integration binaries via the shared TestHarness.init() chokepoint, requiring no binary-specific changes
Fix scope <= 5 files, matches files_to_change in ISS-0107.json (tests/integration/helpers.zig, 1 file)
Independently verify against the live tests/integration/helpers.zig source that the design's factual claims about current lock acquire/release lines are accurate

result.summary: Design in src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md independently verified against the live tests/integration/helpers.zig source and PASSES all Step 2b checks. All cited line numbers/strings are exact: lines 99-100 ('bpm_test_migrations_public' advisory lock, released via defer at end of runMigrations()'s own body), lines 144-145 (per-schema hashtext($1) lock, also released via defer inside runMigrationsForSchema()), resetTestData() at 306-322, applyCompatibilityShims() at 208-296, and TestHarness.init() call sequence at 413-496 (runMigrations:440 -> runMigrationsForSchema:448 -> configureTestSearchPath:457 -> resetTestData:463 -> ensureDefaultOidcSeeds:468 -> applyCompatibilityShims:473 -> conn.begin():487) all match the design's claims exactly. The design correctly addresses the diagnosed root cause (widening the lock's critical section to cover resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims(), currently unprotected) rather than a retry/timeout workaround. Structural change (shape 1: acquire bpm_test_migrations_public before configureTestSearchPath, release after applyCompatibilityShims completes) is unambiguous. No literal Zig diff present -- only prose describing the acquire/release relocation and reusing the existing defer idiom. Lock-key reuse decision (reuse existing key vs new bpm_test_harness_init key) is justified with real reasoning: a second key would only provide exclusivity within its own critical section, not across the migrations vs reset/shim boundary, reopening exactly the kind of cross-phase race (TRUNCATE vs concurrent migration DDL) the fix is meant to close. Performance/serialization tradeoff is explicitly acknowledged (full reset/shim serialization across ~19+ binaries at startup) and justified by direct comparison to the accepted ISS-0106 precedent, with a bounded-cost argument (near-empty test DB, single-table TRUNCATEs, seconds not minutes). Error taxonomy section present and correctly states 'none' -- this is a critical-section boundary move, not a new error path; confirmed function signatures (!void) and existing best-effort error.ServerError handling in truncateTableBestEffort()/execCompatibilitySql() are untouched. Callers/scripts impact correctly identifies all ~19+ test-integration binaries via the shared TestHarness.init() chokepoint requiring zero binary-specific changes, and correctly notes test_iss503_rls_removal.zig is unaffected in either direction -- independently confirmed by reading that file's own doc comment (lines 40-57), which states it opens its own raw pg.Conn entirely outside helpers.zig's advisory-lock machinery and is already serialized by build.zig's barrier from ISS-0106. Fix scope is exactly 1 file (tests/integration/helpers.zig), matching ISS-0107.json's files_to_change. Type E classification is correct per templates/lego-catalog.md: this is cross-cutting concurrency-control logic in a shared test-infra chokepoint, not a CRUD/list-page/migration/React-Flow-node pattern -- no template type applies (rule 5 default). Self-deadlock check (adversarial focus of this review): confirmed via grep that src/db/migrations.zig contains zero pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock calls of its own (Migrations.run()/runForSchema() do no internal locking, consistent with the design's and ISS-0107.json's claim that locking is entirely helpers.zig's caller-side responsibility) -- so widening the outer lock to wrap runMigrationsForSchema() introduces no nested-acquire-of-the-same-key hazard. The per-schema lock at lines 144-145 uses a distinct hashtext() input ('tenant_default' vs 'bpm_test_migrations_public'), and Postgres session-level advisory locks are re-entrant/independent across distinct keys within one session, so nesting it inside the widened outer lock is safe and cannot self-deadlock a single process against itself. No other call site anywhere in the repo acquires bpm_test_migrations_public (grep-confirmed: only helpers.zig:99 acquires it; all other hits are doc-comment prose/design-file references). tools/lint_design_artefact.py src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md: 'OK -- 1 file(s) checked, no issues.'

issues.description: The design's 'Preferred shape' acquire point is described as 'immediately before configureTestSearchPath() is called (i.e. right after runMigrationsForSchema() returns at line 448/451)' -- line 451 does not correspond to any statement inside runMigrationsForSchema() in the current source (that function ends at line 187; line 451 is inside TestHarness.init() itself, roughly the blank/comment line after the runMigrationsForSchema() call at line 448). This is a minor citation imprecision, not a substantive ambiguity -- the intended acquire point (right after the runMigrationsForSchema() call returns control to init(), before configureTestSearchPath() at line 457) is still unambiguous from context and matches the rest of the document. Does not block PASS; BACKEND-DEV should simply place the acquire call between the runMigrationsForSchema() call site (line 448) and the configureTestSearchPath() call site (line 457).
